answer.answer: These are the 25 measures returned with more than half of Texas hospitals missing a score. Measure names are shown as provided (up to 60 characters); total Texas hospitals is 467 for each measure. […]
answer.sql: WITH tx_total AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_hospitals FROM hq.hospitals AS h WHERE h.is_texas), latest AS (SELECT mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id WHERE h.is_texas), score_counts AS (SELECT l.measure_id, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE l.score IS NOT NULL) AS hospitals_with_score FROM latest AS l WHERE l.rn = 1 GROUP BY l.measure_id), missing_rates AS (SELECT m.measure_id, m.domain, LEFT(m.measure_name, 60) AS measure_name, COALESCE(sc.hospitals_with_score, 0) AS hospitals_with_score, tt.total_hospitals, ROUND(CAST((100.0 * (tt.total_hospitals - COALESCE(sc.hospitals_with_score, 0)) / tt.total_hospitals) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS percent_missing FROM hq.measures AS m CROSS JOIN tx_total AS tt LEFT JOIN score_counts AS sc ON UPPER(sc.measure_id) = UPPER(m.measure_id)) SELECT measure_id, domain, measure_name, hospitals_with_score, total_hospitals, percent_missing FROM missing_rates WHERE percent_missing > 50 ORDER BY percent_missing DESC, measure_id LIMIT 25

answer.answer: For each ownership type, the recommend figure is an average hospital rate, not a patient count; the hospital count includes all Texas hospitals of that type, including those without a recommend score. Ordered by average recommend percentage: Government - Local — 11 hospitals, 79.0% recommend, 3.0 average overall stars; Government - State — 15, 79.0%, 3.67 stars; Physician — 27, 78.85%, 3.67 stars; Government - Hospital District or Authority — 78, 75.73%, 2.77 stars; Voluntary non-profit - Other — 18, 74.36%, 3.43 stars; Veterans Health Administration — 5, 74.2%, 4.4 stars; Voluntary non-profit - Private — 134, 73.52%, 3.7 stars; Voluntary non-profit - Church — 5, 73.5%, 3.75 stars; Proprietary — 171, 68.58%, 3.01 stars.
answer.sql: SELECT h.hospital_ownership AS ownership_type, m.measure_id, m.measure_name, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospital_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(latest_recommend.score) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_would_definitely_recommend_pct, ROUND(CAST(AVG(h.overall_rating) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_overall_star_rating FROM hq.hospitals AS h JOIN hq.measures AS m ON UPPER(m.measure_id) = UPPER('H_RECMND_DY') LEFT JOIN (SELECT facility_id, score FROM (SELECT mv.facility_id, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, mv.period_start DESC NULLS LAST) AS period_rank FROM hq.measure_values AS mv WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('H_RECMND_DY') AND UPPER(mv.value_type) = UPPER('answer_percent')) AS ranked_recommend WHERE period_rank = 1) AS latest_recommend ON latest_recommend.facility_id = h.facility_id WHERE UPPER(h.state) = UPPER('TX') GROUP BY h.hospital_ownership, m.measure_id, m.measure_name HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY AVG(latest_recommend.score) DESC NULLS LAST, h.hospital_ownership LIMIT 200

Return the Houston-area hospitals (Harris, Fort Bend, Montgomery, Galveston and Brazoria counties) with their rate and percentile (3 decimals), lowest percentile first, ties by hospital name.
answer.answer: The shown result contains 32 Houston-area hospitals, ordered from lowest to highest national percentile. Their heart failure 30-day death rates range from 6.0 to 12.1, and their percentiles range from 0.004 to 0.711. HOUSTON METHODIST HOSPITAL is lowest (rate 6.0; percentile 0.004), and MEMORIAL HERMANN KATY HOSPITAL is highest (rate 12.1; percentile 0.711).
answer.sql: WITH latest_rows AS (SELECT h.facility_id, h.facility_name, h.county, h.state, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, mv.period_start DESC NULLS LAST) AS period_rank FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('MORT_30_HF')), national_percentiles AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, state, score, PERCENT_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score ASC) AS national_percentile FROM latest_rows WHERE period_rank = 1 AND score IS NOT NULL) SELECT facility_name AS hospital_name, county, score AS heart_failure_30_day_death_rate, ROUND(CAST(national_percentile AS DECIMAL), 3) AS national_percentile FROM national_percentiles WHERE state = 'TX' AND UPPER(county) IN ('HARRIS', 'FORT BEND', 'MONTGOMERY', 'GALVESTON', 'BRAZORIA') ORDER BY national_percentile ASC, facility_name ASC LIMIT 200

answer.sql: SELECT m.measure_id, m.measure_name, COUNT(*) AS texas_hospitals_with_score, MAX(ph.period_count) AS largest_reporting_period_count, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE ph.period_count > 1) AS hospitals_with_multiple_periods FROM hq.measures AS m JOIN (SELECT mv.facility_id, COUNT(DISTINCT (mv.period_start, mv.period_end)) AS period_count FROM hq.measure_values AS mv JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = mv.facility_id WHERE UPPER(mv.measure_id) = UPPER('H_HSP_RATING_9_10') AND mv.score IS NOT NULL AND h.state = 'TX' GROUP BY mv.facility_id) AS ph ON TRUE WHERE UPPER(m.measure_id) = UPPER('H_HSP_RATING_9_10') GROUP BY m.measure_id, m.measure_name LIMIT 200

answer.sql: WITH tx_scores AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, UPPER(measure_id) AS measure_id, score FROM hq.v_tx_latest WHERE UPPER(measure_id) IN ('READM_30_PN', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'SEP_1') AND score IS NOT NULL), measure_stats AS (SELECT measure_id, AVG(score) AS mean_score, STDDEV(score) AS sd_score FROM tx_scores GROUP BY measure_id), hospital_scores AS (SELECT facility_id, facility_name, county, MAX(score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'READM_30_PN') AS pneumonia_readmission, MAX(score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'H_RECMND_DY') AS definitely_recommend, MAX(score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'SEP_1') AS sepsis_care FROM tx_scores GROUP BY facility_id, facility_name, county), stats AS (SELECT MAX(mean_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'READM_30_PN') AS readm_mean, MAX(sd_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'READM_30_PN') AS readm_sd, MAX(mean_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'H_RECMND_DY') AS recommend_mean, MAX(sd_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'H_RECMND_DY') AS recommend_sd, MAX(mean_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'SEP_1') AS sepsis_mean, MAX(sd_score) FILTER(WHERE measure_id = 'SEP_1') AS sepsis_sd FROM measure_stats), composites AS (SELECT h.facility_id, h.facility_name, h.county, ROUND(((s.readm_mean - Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.

answer.question: For six measures, what share of Texas hospitals do better than the national average (average over all U.S. hospitals with a score)? Measures: 30-day pneumonia readmission rate, 30-day heart failure death rate, central-line infection ratio (lower is better for these three), sepsis care percentage, 'would definitely recommend' percentage and HCAHPS summary star rating (higher is better for these three). Return measure ID, the national average (2 decimals), Texas hospitals with a score, how many beat the national average and the share in percent (1 decimal), highest share first, ties by measure ID.
answer.answer: These are averages across U.S. hospitals with a score for each measure, not patient counts. Texas results, ordered by the share beating the national average: HAI_1_SIR (central-line infection ratio): national average 0.58; 151 Texas hospitals with a score, 99 beat it (65.6%). MORT_30_HF (30-day heart failure death rate): 11.07; 206 hospitals, 132 beat it (64.1%). SEP_1 (sepsis care percentage): 63.79; 233 hospitals, 146 beat it (62.7%). READM_30_PN (30-day pneumonia readmission rate): 17.34; 258 hospitals, 150 beat it (58.1%). H_RECMND_DY (would definitely recommend percentage): 71.22; 297 hospitals, 158 beat it (53.2%). H_STAR_RATING (HCAHPS summary star rating): 3.27; 229 hospitals, 92 beat it (40.2%).
answer.sql: WITH ranked_scores AS (SELECT mv.facility_id, mv.measure_id, mv.score, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY mv.facility_id, UPPER(mv.measure_id) ORDER BY mv.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, mv.id DESC) AS rn FROM hq.measure_values AS mv WHERE mv.score IS NOT NULL AND UPPER(mv.measure_id) IN ('READM_30_PN', 'MORT_30_HF', 'HAI_1_SIR', 'SEP_1', 'H_RECMND_DY', 'H_STAR_RATING')), latest_scores AS (SELECT facility_id, measure_id, score FROM ranked_scores WHERE rn = 1), national_averages AS (SELECT UPPER(measure_id) AS measure_key, AVG(score) AS national_avg FROM latest_scores GROUP BY UPPER(measure_id)), texas_counts AS (SELECT UPPER(ls.measure_id) AS measure_key, COUNT(*) AS tx_hospitals_with_score, COUNT(*) FILTER(WHERE (m.higher_is_better AND ls.score > na.national_avg) OR (NOT m.higher_is_better AND ls.score < na.national_avg)) AS tx_beating_national FROM latest_scores AS ls JOIN hq.hospitals AS h ON h.facility_id = ls.facility_id JOIN national_averages AS na ON na.measure_key = UPPER(ls.measure_id) JOIN hq.measures AS m ON UPPER(m.measure_id) = UPPER(ls.measure_id) WHERE h.state = 'TX' GROUP BY UPPER(ls.measure_id)) SELECT m.measure_id, m.measure_name, ROUND(CAST(na.national_avg AS DECIMAL), 2) AS national_average, tc.tx_hospitals_with_score, tc.tx_beating_national, ROUND(100.0 * tc.tx_beating_national / NULLIF(tc.tx_hospitals_with_score, 0), 1) AS share_beating_pct FROM national_averages AS na JOIN texas_counts AS tc ON tc.measure_key = na.measure_key JOIN hq.measures AS m ON UPPER(m.measure_id) = na.measure_key ORDER BY share_beating_pct DESC, m.measure_id LIMIT 200
